short: The smallest quantity a supplier will accept in one order.
seoTitle: Minimum Order Quantity — Meaning and Example for Businesses
metaDescription: Minimum order quantity, or MOQ, is the smallest quantity a supplier is willing to sell in a single order. Part of the free Setu business glossary.
definition: Minimum order quantity, or MOQ, is the smallest quantity a supplier is willing to sell in a single order. It exists to make production or delivery worthwhile for them, and it constrains how finely a buyer can order.
bodyHtml:
Why Minimum Order Quantity matters

A high MOQ on a slow-moving item creates dead stock by design. It is often the real reason a shop has three years of some SKU sitting in the back.

How Minimum Order Quantity works in practice

Compare the MOQ against your monthly usage before agreeing to stock a line. Where the MOQ exceeds a few months of sales, negotiate, share the order with another buyer, or decline the line.

faq.question: Can MOQs be negotiated?
faq.answer: Often yes, especially for a first order or in exchange for a longer commitment on faster-moving lines.

faq.question: How do I judge whether an MOQ is acceptable?
faq.answer: Divide it by expected monthly usage. More than about three months of cover is usually a warning.
